title: 半山面包：一个面包店首页的三种开法
Banshan Bakery: three ways to open a bakery's page
summary: 同一家面包店、同一套品牌 token，分别把今日库存、明早预订或店铺故事放在首屏。
The same bakery under the same brand tokens, leading with today's stock, tomorrow's orders, or the shop's story.
brief: 为一家面包店的单页网站出三版：看今天剩什么、到店信息、预订明早。页面是纯 HTML 和 CSS，没有构建步骤；品牌色和字体已在 style.css 里定义。

Three directions for a bakery's one-page site: what is left today, how to visit, and ordering for tomorrow. Plain HTML and CSS with no build step; the brand colours and font are already set in style.css.

optimizes: 库存先行：首屏就是今日面包板，剩余数量用大字和小方块显示，售罄项划掉并直接给出‘明早可预订’；预订栏在桌面端常驻右侧，手机端有固定底栏跳转。

Stock first: the first screen is today's bread board, with remaining counts in large type and small squares; sold-out items are struck through and offer 'order for tomorrow' right there. The order panel stays on the right on desktop; phones get a fixed bottom bar that jumps to it.
tradeoff: 品牌故事和标语被压成一行，第一次来的访客对这家店的了解最少；底部固定条占用手机屏幕空间。
The brand story and tagline shrink to one line, so a first-time visitor learns the least about the shop; the fixed bottom bar takes phone screen space.
bestFor: 老客户上午在手机上反复查看‘还有没有’，并在售罄后立刻改订明早。
Regulars checking 'is there any left' on their phones in the morning, and switching to tomorrow's order the moment something sells out.

alt: 今日面包板在首屏，剩余数量用小方块显示，右侧是预订栏和到店信息
Today's bread board first, remaining counts as small squares, the order panel and visiting information on the right

optimizes: 预订转化：单栏一张表单，先选明早要的面包和数量（今日剩余作为括号内的参考信息），再填手机号和日期，底部实时汇总‘明早取 × 共 ¥’。

Order conversion: one single-column form that first picks tomorrow's loaves and quantities (today's remaining stock shown in brackets as a reference), then phone number and date, with a live total at the bottom: 'pick up tomorrow × total ¥'.
tradeoff: 表单从两个字段变成按款预订，店里要按单备货、核对数量，运营成本上升；到店信息被推到页面末尾。
The form grows from two fields to per-loaf ordering, so the shop has to prepare and check quantities per order, which raises operating cost; visiting information is pushed to the end of the page.
bestFor: 供不应求、希望把当天的产量尽量提前订掉的阶段，或者准备上线按款预订流程时。
When demand outstrips supply and the shop wants the day's output ordered ahead, or when it is about to launch per-loaf ordering.

alt: 单栏表单，按款选数量，下面填手机号和取货日期
A single-column form: quantities per loaf, then phone number and pickup date

optimizes: 到店与品牌印象：大字标题和两段店铺叙事放在前面，地址可点开地图，营业时间做成七天表并标出今天，面包用点线菜单排版，预订收尾。

Visiting and brand impression: a large headline and two paragraphs of the shop's story come first, the address opens a map, opening hours are a seven-day table with today marked, the breads are set as a dotted menu, and ordering closes the page.
tradeoff: 库存和预订都在首屏之下，手机上要滚两三屏才能下单；页面更长，信息密度最低。
Stock and ordering both sit below the first screen, so a phone has to scroll two or three screens to order; the page is longer and the least dense.
bestFor: 新店宣传、被分享到社交媒体时的落地页，或者访客大多是第一次来、想先知道这是一家什么店。
A new shop's publicity, a landing page shared on social media, or visitors who are mostly first-timers and want to know what kind of shop this is.

alt: 大字标题和店铺叙事在前，下面是地址、营业时间表和点线菜单
A large headline and the shop's story first, then the address, opening hours and a dotted menu

reason: 原页面的信息里最会变、最被反复查看的是‘剩几个 / 已售罄’，A 把它做成首屏主体，预订栏常驻一旁，老客户在手机上一屏能完成‘看库存—订明早’。这是基于页面已有信息结构的推断；A 是否真的提高预订量、B 的逐款预订是否被店里接受，都还没有测试。

What changes most and gets checked most on the original page is how many are left and what is sold out. A makes that the body of the first screen and keeps the order panel beside it, so a regular can go from checking stock to ordering for tomorrow on one phone screen. This is inferred from the page's existing information structure; whether A actually raises orders, and whether the shop would accept B's per-loaf ordering, has not been tested.

prompt: 使用完整 Variant Design 技能。在当前项目中先检查页面结构和设计系统，再生成保留核心任务的 A/B/C 三个设计方向。已有品牌保持字体与 tokens；没有品牌约束时探索三种鲜明风格。打开三版预览，说明优化、取舍与适用场景，并给出有理由的推荐，但先不要替我选定最终方案。（这是无人值守运行：不要启动常驻服务器，生成可直接打开的预览文件即可。）

Use the full Variant Design skill. In this project, first check the page structure and design system, then generate three design directions A/B/C that keep the core task. Keep the fonts and tokens of an existing brand; without brand constraints, explore three distinct styles. Open the three previews, explain what each optimizes, trades off and suits, and recommend one with reasons, but do not choose the final direction for me yet. (This is an unattended run: do not start a long-running server; preview files that open directly are enough.)
